My understanding of it is this: Fast Track authorization was for the deliberation phase of the agreement. Congress could vote "Yes" or "No" with no option to insert riders or modify clauses in order to simplify negotiations. Now that the text has been "agreed" to and signed, congress will have to draft bills enacting all the thousands of changes contained in the agreement's text with a deadline of 2 years for full legal implementation by a certain percentage of the signing countries or else the agreement is null and void. Congress has the opportunity to insert riders and other congressional fuckery into the bills which work to align our specific legal system (or reject the changes) during this period of time between signing and the agreement entering effect.

At this point, the only road to not getting the TPP is to have a sufficient portion of signing countries decline to implement the required legislation.
